prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2015 manifesto sets out a plan to make Britain work for working people, anchored by a Budget Responsibility Lock: every promise is fully funded with no new borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year; national debt will fall and the current budget return to surplus as soon as possible, independently verified by the OBR. The core belief: Britain only succeeds when working families succeed—through fair rewards for work, strong public services, and power devolved to communities.

Economic foundations and fair taxes
- Restore fiscal credibility while tackling the causes of the deficit through higher productivity and rising living standards.
- Fairer taxes: restore the 50p top rate; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance; abolish non-dom status; no rises in basic or higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; tough action on avoidance.
- Back small business: cut and then freeze business rates for 1.5m small firms; create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; boost competition in banking; levy payday lenders to support credit unions.
- Long-term growth: National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 with cost control and better northern rail; strategic roads and cycling; swift airport decision; universal affordable high-speed broadband and better mobile coverage.
- Lead the low-carbon transition: legal 2030 decarbonised power target; empower the Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; one million new green jobs.

Better work, pay and chances for young people
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to £8+ by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and Make Work Pay contracts; require listed firms to report Living Wage status.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts and close the agency worker loophole; scrap employment tribunal fees.
- Rebalance corporate governance to favour long-termism, curb excessive pay, and give employees a voice.
- Create a gold-standard technical route: Technical Baccalaureate and Technical Degrees; guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; cut tuition fees to £6,000; end unpaid internships lock-out. Fund a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee via a bank bonus tax.

Cutting the cost of living and fixing broken markets
- Freeze energy bills until 2017 and reform the market with a tough new watchdog; drive energy efficiency.
- Water affordability scheme and stronger regulation.
- Rail reform with a public operator option; fare freeze then strict caps; powers for city/region-wide integrated transport.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; new garden cities; tackle land banking.
- Fair renting: three-year tenancies the norm, cap excessive rent rises, ban letting fees. Abolish the Bedroom Tax.
- Family support: free childcare rising from 15 to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4-year-olds; guarantee wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to four weeks and increase pay.

World-class NHS and care, and high-quality education
- Rescue the NHS: 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 more GPs, 3,000 more midwives funded by a Mansion Tax, a tobacco levy and anti-avoidance; 48-hour GP appointments; one-week cancer tests.
- Repeal the Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; focus on prevention.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; support carers.
- Protect the entire education budget; all teachers qualified; cap infant class sizes at 30; new School Standards Directors; boost vocational excellence.

Safe, cohesive communities with fair immigration
- Protect neighbourhood policing (safeguard over 10,000 officers); a Victims’ Law; tougher action on domestic abuse and child exploitation; ban legal highs.
- Counter extremism with community-led Prevent, stronger oversight, and proportionate powers.
- Controlled, fair immigration: 1,000 extra border staff, full exit checks, two-year wait for benefits, English requirement for public-facing roles; ban wage undercutting and rogue agencies.

Power closer to people and rights protected
- English Devolution Act: £30bn and major powers to city and county regions; local Public Accounts Committees; Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; votes at 16.
- Clean politics: tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; extend FOI; media plurality and full Leveson implementation; protect the Human Rights Act; require large firms to publish gender pay gaps; race equality strategy. Keep Channel 4 public; free museum entry; give fans a voice in football clubs.

Britain in the world
- Reform the EU from within; lock any future power transfers behind a referendum; uphold NATO; defence review; maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent; strengthen cyber security.
- Lead on climate change towards global net zero in the second half of the century.
- Keep 0.7% aid, focus on the poorest, support universal health coverage.

A fully funded, credible plan to rebuild a fairer, more secure Britain—together.

TEXT_C:
Stronger for Scotland: The SNP vows to shake up an out‑of‑touch Westminster so it serves Scotland better. A vote SNP is a vote to make Scotland’s voice heard, for progressive politics, and to end austerity. The SNP will never put the Tories into power; if there’s an anti‑Tory majority, it will work with others to lock them out and press Labour to deliver real change. We believe in independence, but this election is about making Scotland stronger at Westminster.

Public finances and growth: Replace austerity with modest annual spending increases, while having borrowing and debt fall as a share of income. Invest in infrastructure, productivity and jobs; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund; seed‑fund the Scottish Business Development Bank. Ensure the better‑off contribute a little more (restore 50p top rate; tax bankers’ bonuses; bank levy; mansion tax; end non‑doms; tackle avoidance).

Better off with the SNP: Protect the NHS from privatisation and secure an extra £2bn for Scotland’s NHS by 2020‑21. Raise the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; expand Modern Apprenticeships to 30,000; widen EMA. Increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level; raise Universal Credit work allowance; retain the pension triple lock with a £160 single‑tier pension and review the rise to state pension age 67. Cut household energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation and forcing pass‑through of wholesale price cuts. Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP roll‑out and reverse the DLA→PIP change; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments; protect disability support; end exploitative zero‑hours contracts.

Jobs and investment: Boost capital spending; connect Scotland to HS2 from north and south; accelerate broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation; target 100,000 UK affordable homes per year; devolve and cut APD, consider a VAT cut for hospitality; expand export finance. Back creative industries with a fair BBC Scotland share (+£100m) and support for games; stabilise the Annual Investment Allowance; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000. Shape immigration to Scotland’s needs, including restoring post‑study work visas. Ensure small firms are paid on time.

Energy, climate and environment: Lead on carbon reduction and climate justice. Expand offshore wind and grid upgrades; support onshore wind, hydro, CCS and heat; grow community energy; maintain a fracking moratorium. Oppose new nuclear and block Trident renewal, redirecting billions to services. Protect species and end the ivory trade.

Rebalancing the UK and rural fairness: Invest in northern infrastructure and city deals; create a Scottish Cities Fund; secure Scotland’s fair CAP convergence share; protect Royal Mail’s USO and public interest stake; deliver rural fuel fairness; devolve food levies; return Crown Estate seabed revenues to coastal communities.

Rights, democracy and privacy: Promote fair work and the living wage; mandate equal pay audits; strengthen maternity protections. Scrap the House of Lords; adopt STV; effective MP recall; votes at 16–17. Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; remove VAT on sanitary products; let charities campaign. Oppose mass surveillance; back targeted, overseen powers.

Security, foreign affairs and EU: Strengthen Scotland’s conventional defence footprint and shipbuilding; improve care for service personnel; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy. Ensure any military action is UN‑lawful and Parliament‑approved. Recognise Palestine. Keep the UK in the EU; oppose Brexit and require a “double majority” in any referendum; exempt the NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP.

Home Rule: Deliver Smith in full and go further to full fiscal responsibility. Prioritise devolution of employment, welfare, business taxes, National Insurance and equalities—without UK vetoes—retaining Barnett in transition.

Record and pledge: SNP government has strengthened the NHS, improved schools, cut crime with 1,000 extra police, frozen Council Tax and mitigated Tory welfare cuts. On May 7, vote SNP to make Scotland’s voice heard and deliver a fairer, more prosperous, anti‑austerity UK.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_F" | "TEXT_C"
}
